candidates.title: PhiCube: a reconfigurable bilateral robotic device for neurorehabilitation
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Neuromotor disorders affecting upper-limb function represent a substantial clinical challenge in pediatric populations, with conditions such as hemiplegic cerebral palsy imposing lasting limitations on functional independence and quality of life. Bilateral motor training has emerged as a neurophysiologically grounded paradigm, offering functional advantages over purely unilateral approaches by actively exploiting interlimb coordination mechanisms. Despite the growing evidence base for bilateral training, existing robotic devices present critical limitations in kinematic reconfigurability, parameterizable inter-limb coupling, and portability, restricting their clinical accessibility and therapeutic versatility, particularly in pediatric settings. Methods: This paper introduces PhiCube, a modular robotic platform engineered for bilateral upper-limb neuromotor rehabilitation in pediatric populations. The device architecture is built around a compact central body housing two independent motorized rotational joints, whose actuation axes can be rapidly aligned with any of the three principal anatomical planes through a dedicated reconfiguration mechanism. A set of interchangeable therapeutic manipulanda, each eliciting distinct motor patterns, extends the device's therapeutic scope across the proximal-to-distal upper-limb kinematic chain. The bilateral coupling controller is formulated as an impedance-based scheme exposing tuneable parameters governing the kinematic transmission ratio between limbs, the directional asymmetry of the coupling, and the bilateral assistance level. A gamification environment embeds motor training within interactive paradigms designed for pediatric engagement, with real-time mapping between game trajectories and robotic assistance references. Kinematic simulations were conducted within the OpenSim framework, integrating an upper-extremity musculoskeletal model through a custom Python-based inverse kinematics pipeline. Results: Kinematic simulations confirmed that each handle-orientation combination elicits a distinct and characterizable pattern of joint recruitment across the upper-limb kinematic chain, with configurations ranging from isolated distal training (wrist flexion-extension, forearm pronation-supination) to compound multi-joint synergies engaging the shoulder, elbow, and wrist simultaneously. Analysis of the bilateral controller through contour mapping of the torque field demonstrated that the coupling parameters shape the inter-limb interaction, spanning configurations from unilateral guidance-in which one limb drives the other without reciprocal constraint-to fully symmetric bilateral coupling, and from in-phase synchronous to counter-phase alternating coordination. Discussion: The parametric characterization of both the kinematic architecture and the control space provides objective evidence that PhiCube can address a broad and clinically relevant spectrum of bilateral rehabilitation paradigms, from proximal multi-joint synergies to isolated distal training, and from strict guided-movement to symmetric and counter-phase bilateral coordination. These properties position PhiCube as a versatile tool for neuromotor rehabilitation, where therapeutic goals, residual motor capacity, and anthropometric constraints vary substantially across patients and evolve throughout the course of treatment.

candidates.title: Understanding how movement signals shape early social coordination and learning
candidates.abstract: From early in life, social interactions rely on a rich exchange of nonverbal information. This review paper focuses on the nonverbal, kinematic information conveyed by how social partners move and proposes that such movement modulations may facilitate interpersonal coordination between infants and adults, as well as support infants' learning in early interactions. So far, findings on movement modulations have been investigated in isolation: sensorimotor communication in interpersonal coordination between adults (signaling) on the one hand, and in early teaching interactions between adults and infants (motionese) on the other. This paper integrates these findings and argues that both forms of movement-based communication operate along a continuum of predictability and surprise, which are flexibly adapted depending on the underlying social goal, i.e., interpersonal coordination or teaching. This leads to testable hypotheses on how predictability and surprise in adult movements could support infants' real-time action prediction and, consequently, their learning and optimization of interpersonal coordination, with a potential impact on social development in the long run. By integrating empirical findings from distinct research lines, the present review offers a novel framework to investigate how early social interactions and learning may be shaped by movement-based communication, opening new avenues for exploring developmental trajectories.

candidates.title: Humanoid robots in the operating room: a framework for staged integration of embodied AI in surgery
candidates.abstract: The next leap in surgical innovation may not come from refining precision but from embodied AI transforming the operating room (OR) itself. We contend that intelligent humanoid agents, owing to their anthropomorphic design, may enter the OR through a staged deployment framework from pre-clinical validation to low-risk tasks before progressively advancing toward elevated-risk assistive roles, providing a pathway for integration of embodied AI autonomy in critical environments. This perspective examines how generalist embodied AI may realistically be integrated into the OR, and explores the pathways, challenges, and implications this holds for the future of surgical care.

candidates.title: Steganographic Sexualization: Sustained Socio-Technicality In Online Child Sexual Exploitation And Abuse Communities
candidates.abstract: Though dedicated task forces commonly target individual child sexual exploitation and abuse (CSEA) files and offenders, this paper views them as components of systematically formed and maintained communities. Reviewing the existing body of literature reveals that researchers rarely bridge the interdisciplinary fields contributing to the sociotechnical phenomena of CSEA communities (CSEACs) and therefore cannot accurately identify their cross-functional characteristics, nor investigate how they coevolve and reinforce each other. Multi-method qualitative data analysis adapts insights from both traditional and digital spheres, synthesizes them with communication theories, and bridges disparate studies. Its holistic perspective identifies dynamics between offenders, media, and their digital environments that strategically enforce control, transform individual abstractions into collective realities, and create frameworks for abuse. Consequently, this study reveals inherent vulnerabilities in CSEAC structures applicable for intelligence targeting.

candidates.title: The bare life of weeds: A biopolitics of AI and robotic agricultural Weed Technologies
candidates.abstract: As conventional chemical methods of weed control come under increasing scrutiny, the agri-tech industry has turned to artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics to combat the evolving ‘weed problem’. However, the intervention of AI and robotics into agricultural weed management in this ‘post-herbicide’ era poses new questions for human-weed relations. Although attention has been paid to the social and ethical impacts of agricultural AI and robotics in general, there has been less focus on its nonhuman impacts, in particular, the consequences for weed and plant life. Therefore, this paper examines AI and robotic agricultural weed systems and asks how it reproduces new biopolitical norms for human-weed relations under changing technological conditions. I review the literature on AI and robotic weed technologies, in addition to broader social science scholarship of weeds, to argue that the turn to AI and robotics is a biopolitical move that reconfigures the capital-colonial categorisation of agricultural weeds and thus forecloses sustainable agri-futures. I demonstrate how AI and robotics reshape biopolitical norms of weeds based on a logic of immunity which works to program weeds as ‘bare life’ and, in turn, enable the industrial expansion of new weed technologies by further legitimating the indiscriminate eradication of uncommodifiable plant life. In doing so, I briefly propose relations with weeds through an affirmative biopolitics to unsettle the technocratic categorisations of weeds and make visible their status as vital beings for collaborative and multispecies futures.

candidates.title: The Effect of Gamified Robotic Activities on Gifted Student
candidates.abstract: This study aims to explore how gamified robotics activities affect the cognitive and affective skills of gifted students. Using a mixed-methods design, it employed a straightforward experimental setup with a single group, measuring before and after the intervention. The research examined cognitive flexibility, computational thinking, motivation, and satisfaction throughout the process. The sample included 24 gifted middle school students. Data collection involved the player type determination scale, the middle school computational thinking scale, the cognitive flexibility scale, written opinion, and observational forms during activities. The activities, based on design principles, were carried out using LEGO EV3 educational robot kits. Results showed no significant change in cognitive competencies from pre- to post-test. However, students were actively engaged, and gamification elements boosted their motivation and satisfaction. Fun content positively influenced students, though challenges such as competition, coding difficulties, and intra-group conflicts were also noted.

candidates.title: A human-centered cognitive support framework for manual industrial assembly: integrating perception, agentic reasoning, and augmented reality guidance
candidates.abstract: Abstract Manual industrial assembly remains essential in high-variety and customized production, but increasing product and process complexity places substantial cognitive demands on operators. Existing assistance systems, particularly augmented reality-based solutions, improve instruction visualization and task guidance, yet they often remain weakly connected to the real assembly state and limited in reasoning, adaptation, and decision support. This paper proposes a human-centered cognitive support framework for manual industrial assembly that integrates perception, agentic reasoning, knowledge grounding, and augmented reality guidance. The study is informed by a systematic search, bibliometric overview, and literature analysis of 129 Scopus-indexed documents. The analysis shows that augmented reality dominates current cognitive support approaches, while AI-based methods are increasingly used for object recognition, contextual interpretation, adaptive information delivery, and error detection. However, perception, reasoning, guidance, and knowledge grounding are still commonly treated as isolated functions. Based on these findings, 11 review-derived design requirements are formulated and used to develop a conceptual perception-cognition-guidance framework that represents cognitive support as a closed human-centered loop grounded in procedures, constraints, rules, and memory. The framework is then translated into a layered implementation architecture comprising physical, perception, cognitive, guidance, knowledge, and application layers. Structured data contracts clarify how sensory and interaction data can be transformed into perception evidence, structured assembly states, cognitive support decisions, and device-specific guidance commands. A toy-train assembly demonstrator illustrates how procedural state modeling, multi-camera perception, YOLO11-based object detection, projector-based guidance, and contract-based data exchange can connect physical assembly events with structured reasoning and operator-facing feedback.

candidates.title: A Semantic Web Approach for Integrating Portuguese Open Government Data as Linked Open Data
candidates.abstract: Open Government Data (OGD) has become an important instrument for promoting transparency, accountability, and citizen participation in democratic institutions.However, despite the increasing availability of governmental datasets, information published by Portuguese public institutions remains fragmented across multiple sources, heterogeneous formats, and isolated data silos.This fragmentation limits interoperability, complicates data reuse, and creates significant barriers for developers, researchers, journalists, and citizens seeking to analyse governmental activity.This dissertation addresses these challenges through the design and implementation of a Linked Open Data (LOD) infrastructure for Portuguese parliamentary information.The proposed solution aggregates data from heterogeneous governmental sources, namely the Assembleia da República, into a unified knowledge graph based on Semantic Web technologies.To achieve this, a Linked Data Application Profile (LDAP) was developed to model parliamentary entities, activities, and relationships while reusing established vocabularies and standards whenever possible.Data extraction, transformation, validation, and integration are performed through an automated pipeline capable of processing multiple source formats and generating standards-compliant RDF representations.The resulting knowledge graph enriches parliamentary data through semantic relationships, entity reconciliation, and interoperability mechanisms that enable cross-dataset analysis and integration with external knowledge bases.In addition, change detection mechanisms are employed to maintain data freshness and reduce the maintenance burden traditionally associated with custom data integration solutions.The infrastructure is further validated through a case study involving PoliTrack, demonstrating how downstream applications can consume the knowledge graph as a reusable data source rather than relying on bespoke extraction and transformation pipelines.The results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves the accessibility, interoperability, and reusability of Portuguese governmental data while facilitating the development of transparencyoriented applications and advanced analytical queries.The developed infrastructure resulted in a knowledge graph containing 1.688.632RDF triples, covering five parliamentary legislatures, and enabled entity reconciliation through 35 owl:sameAs links.By transforming fragmented governmental datasets into a semantically rich and interconnected resource, this work contributes to the advancement of open government initiatives and provides a foundation for future civic technology applications built upon Linked Open Data principles.

candidates.title: Finance Corridor: Canonical Operator Definition and Institutional Instrumentation Layer v3 – Worked Historical Example, Provisional Functional Form, and Grounded Open Items
candidates.abstract: This manuscript proposes an institutional instrumentation layer beneath the published Finance Super Corridor defined in Appendix E of the Volume IV Instrumentation Handbook. It supplies concrete telemetry source mappings for six institutional nodes, a branch-and-reconverge causal topology with explicit critical-path logic, a complete worked mapping of the canonical 1974 Herstatt Bank failure through the full operator stack, and a provisional threshold-driven functional form for the corridor-level rupture operator R(Φ)(t). The work also introduces a non-linear threshold-switch mechanism for inter-corridor feedback edges that better captures discrete market shocks and provides explicitly grounded open items for the next iteration, including the undefined reliability aggregation path, Quant Fund/Asset Manager taxonomy gaps, and empirical calibration of the sensitivity (α) and collapse threshold (β) parameters. All extensions are offered as candidate structural hypotheses for stress-testing and collaborative calibration while maintaining strict consistency with the published canon. The manuscript forms part of the broader SCFL / UCMS coherence measurement framework. Status: For Zenodo publication and external review — additive to, not a revision of, the published Handbook. candidates.title: Production and leadership in the creation of a videogame inspired by EPIC: The Musical
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this Final Degree Project is to examine and record the creation process of a turn-based RPG video game based on the narrative universe of “Epic: The Musical” by Jorge Rivera-Herrans. The project was carried out within a multidisciplinary team where the main goal is to understand the organizational and coordination dynamics required to create an indie video game, highlighting the relevance of time management, communication, and motivation in a collaborative environment. A fundamental aspect of the work focuses on the psychological dimension of development, particularly on the leadership and management of a group operating without direct economic compensation. This study addresses how to preserve the motivation, unity, and commitment of the members, and investigates the role of the leader as an organizer, creative guide, and group facilitator. The project methodology stems from the principles of Agile production, but a linear execution had to be abandoned to become a survival system in the face of constant roadblocks. The use of tools such as Jira ceases to be a rigid process and instead acts as a mechanism for flexibility and task reallocation. In this context, this thesis analyzes the critical impact of time volatility in university teams, practically documenting the management of a 37,5% attrition rate (three critical dropouts during the intermediate phase) and the consequent restructuring of the video game's scope to guarantee its viability. To sustain this crisis environment, internal agreements on roles and responsibilities were implemented, in addition to having the support of mentorships from industry professionals who helped with competences, providing responses for the team in the face of problems. The conclusions of the study demonstrate that, in the unpaid indie development ecosystem, the human factor and leadership transcend simple task management to become vital mechanisms for survival. The success of this project does not lie in having executed a perfect plan, but rather in having applied an agile and empathetic management capable of mitigating the constant risk of abandonment, dynamically adapting the game scope in the face of availability crises, and protecting both the team's intrinsic motivation and the legal viability of the product.

candidates.title: CRAFT: a 3D-printed modular design library for task-specific continuum robots
candidates.abstract: Continuum robots offer safe and adaptive interaction through body compliance, yet this same property often limits their load-bearing capability. Addressing this design tradeoff typically requires application-specific designs with long development cycles. We introduce CRAFT, a 3D-printed modular design library for tendon-driven continuum robots that enables rapid mechanical reconfiguration to achieve task-specific stiffness and morphology. The library comprises six interchangeable modules with distinct stiffness profiles, directional compliance, and degrees of freedom, which can be stacked and reconfigured within minutes using inexpensive components. Each module’s behavior under bending, axial, and torsional loading is experimentally characterized. We demonstrate the generality of the approach through three representative robots: a reconfigured long teleoperated probe for aircraft-wing inspection (achieving a 41% reduction in sag), a pipe-crawling robot for confined environments (capable of navigating a 90 ∘ bend and a 30 ∘ incline), and a soft robotic hand for fragile object manipulation (achieving an 85% success rate in an egg-cracking task). Together, these results show how task-specific mechanical properties can be realized through modular composition rather than bespoke redesign, positioning CRAFT as a reusable modular design library for rapidly adaptable continuum robots.

candidates.title: RSP-M/CNX: A Governed Loop-Context Compiler for Delta-Propagated Agentic Workflows
candidates.abstract: Publication context: Carlonoscopen Journal of Coherence Intelligence (CJCI), Volume 1, Issue 18. This paper introduces RSP-M/CNX as a governed loop-context compiler for repeated agentic workflows. RSP-M, or Regenerable Structural Prompt Metabolization, transforms stable workflow doctrine into semantic bindings, preserves exact obligations as literal islands, represents repeated procedures as loop macros, and communicates current work through sealed delta packets. CNX provides the authority-separation boundary: RSP-M optimizes context handling, while policy, validation, audit, and human approval govern action. The paper describes a local-first, machine-readable reference scaffold supporting JSON/YAML schemas, command-line validation, packet sealing, strict manifests, compatibility adapters, machine-checked literal-island hashing, public-release profiles, pilot templates, and custody-idempotent tests. Local validation of the Phase 0B.2 artifact reported 85/85 scaffold tests and 28/28 hardened-procedure tests passing, with manifest verification passing before and after tests. The reported context-reduction values are artifact-level engineering estimates from character counts in one documented development workflow. They are not provider-side token, billing, latency, GPU-utilization, or energy measurements. The paper does not claim production deployment, formal compiler equivalence, universal cost reduction, or measured energy savings. The accompanying ZIP package contains the CJCI/Zenodo publication files, peer-review memo, public/IP posture, no-overclaim statement, evidence map, manifest, and checksum records.

candidates.title: Curio: Enabling Accessible AI and Robotics Education Through a Low-Cost Mobile Robot
candidates.abstract: This innovative practice full paper presents Curio, an innovative, cost-effective, smartphone-integrated robotics platform designed to lower the entry barrier to robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) education. Student engagement is one of the key challenges in robotics and AI education. Tangible learning approaches, such as educational robots, provide an effective way to enhance engagement and learning by offering real-world applications to bridge the gap between theory and practice. However, existing platforms often face barriers such as high cost or limited capabilities. With an estimated parts cost of around $50, Curio is more affordable than similar platforms. By leveraging smartphones, Curio eliminates the need for onboard processing units, dedicated cameras, and additional sensors while maintaining the ability to perform educational tasks. To explore the impact of Curio we conducted a pilot study with 20 participants, where we examined usability, perceived engagement, and potential for integrating into robotics education. The findings indicate high perceived engagement and motivation levels across all participants. Additionally, 95% of participants reported an improvement in their understanding of robotics. Findings suggest that using a robotic system such as Curio can enhance engagement and hands-on learning in robotics and AI education. All resources and projects with Curio will be available at trycurio.com.

candidates.title: Large Language Models as Phenomenotechniques for Linguistics
candidates.abstract: With the help of Bachelard’s concept of phenomenotechnique – meaning an artificial, technological set-up that forces a certain part of reality to reveal itself in a way that can be scientifically observed – this paper tries to theorize large language models (LLMs) as a kind of “epistemological mirrors” that make symbolic language (as a foundation of culture) observable in an unprecedented way. Consequently, LLMs have (besides their known and attested commercial value) immense epistemological value for the humanities since they allow for an alternative way of studying language learning, generation, and structure that can supplement classic linguistic techniques. LLMs can thus be used to reassess the relevance of existing linguistic theories and update them as well as to start developing new theories of language. The paper develops its thesis through a refutation of a common objection to LLMs – that they have no “true” understanding of language since they possess no relation to the outside world – and by showing that real-world relations are irrelevant for human language as well. Consequently, linguistic theories (such as structuralism) that understood language outside of such a framework are once again relevant for a new understanding of symbolic language and culture that LLMs allow.

candidates.title: LLM-driven behavior generation and negotiation for collective robotic construction
candidates.abstract: Abstract Agent-based modeling and simulation (ABMS) has been widely employed to study emergent processes in collective robotic construction (CRC), where global architectural structures arise from local agent interactions. While these approaches reveal how complex assemblies can emerge without centralized control, they remain limited when an architectural goal is known but the behaviors required to achieve it are not. Most CRC workflows still depend on handcrafted heuristics. This paper presents a hybrid CRC workflow that integrates large language models (LLM) into the ABMS behavior design process. The system enables human–AI co-creation of robot behaviors, allowing an LLM agent to generate and negotiate behavioral strategies toward user-defined construction goals under partial observability. The approach is evaluated in simulation, comparing an LLM–heuristic hybrid against a heuristic-only baseline behavior. For well-documented swarm patterns, the LLM matches heuristic performance; for geometrically novel tasks, handcrafted heuristics retain an advantage. By embedding language-based reasoning within ABMS, this work expands participation in CRC behavior design and demonstrates a pathway for translating high-level design intent into adaptive, goal-oriented multiagent construction processes.

candidates.title: Improvement in tomato productivity through a novel wireless based automated drip irrigation system design
candidates.abstract: The present study was conducted to design, develop and evaluate a wireless-based automated drip irrigation system for improving the productivity of tomato crop. Various independent and dependent parameters were considered in design of automated drip irrigation system. The field trial included soil analysis, experimental layout, evaluation of drip system and crop under different irrigation treatments. The highest yield was recorded in wireless irrigation system with treated fruit processing wastewater during both the years of study. In wireless irrigation system, crop irrigated with pressure compensating dripper (PC) has an average yield of 377.97 q ha-¹which is higher as compared to non-pressure compensating dripper (NPC) (364.65 q ha-1). Under the treatments involving the use of fruit processing wastewater in the tomato crop, the percentage of protein, moisture content, carbohydrates, lycopene and sugar increased as compared to those under groundwater irrigation. Treatments comprising of fruit processing wastewater recorded higher dry matter accumulation (6.67 %) and more amounts of lycopene (4.50 mg/100 g) as compared to ground water treated plots. The study revealed that the automated drip irrigation system is an efficient irrigation approach, as it reduces water, labour, energy, time and fertiliser use.

candidates.title: Consumer Reactions to Virtual Influencer Transgressions: How Anime-Looking and AI-Driven Influencers Are Less Vulnerable
candidates.abstract: Virtual influencers in diverse appearances emerged and gained popularity on virtual platforms. However, how the appearances of virtual influencers affect consumers’ attitudes and reactions remained largely unexplored. Through three experimental studies, this paper examines the psychological mechanism and boundary conditions for consumer reactions to virtual influencer transgressions. The results show that consumers are less forgiving and more negative in their reactions to transgressions conducted by human-like virtual influencers compared to anime-like ones, regardless of the type of transgression or the gender of the virtual influencer (Studies 1 and 2). Additionally, the driving mechanism of the virtual influencers has a moderating effect. When consumers are informed that the virtual influencer transgression is driven by a real person rather than AI, the impact of appearance on the reactions to transgressions is aggravated (Study 3). The result shows that appearance and driving mechanism both influence consumer perceptions of the virtual influencers’ agency, thereby determining the degree of reaction to transgressions.

candidates.title: Between conceived and lived spaces: negotiating urban informality in Hanoi’s post-socialist housing
candidates.abstract: While Hanoi’s Collective Living Quarters (KTTs) are often analyzed architecturally, the social dynamics and grassroots strategies of their residents remain under-explored. As artifacts of socialist urbanism, KTTs serve as critical sites for observing the friction between rigid state planning (conceived space) and fluid daily practices (lived space). Utilizing ethnographic fieldwork, this article investigates how residents exercise “spatial agency” to navigate and reshape their environments within urban informality. Drawing on Henri Lefebvre’s production of space theory and Global South perspectives, the study identifies three mechanisms of spatial negotiation. First, residents appropriate thresholds, enclosing semi-public corridors through micro-community consensus to manage high-density living. Second, they produce “gray spaces” via vertical expansion (“tiger cages”), a practice governed by a informal ‘vertical social contract’ between neighbors rather than formal legal codes. Third, the management of contested commons (shared yards) relies on “temporal zoning”, balancing economic livelihoods with communal order. The article argues that the perceived “disorder” of KTTs is actually a sophisticated form of informal governance and resilient adaptation to post-socialist urban transitions. By dismantling the public-private dichotomy, this research reveals how communities reclaim the right to produce lived space by rewriting the architectural scripts of aging socialist infrastructures.

candidates.title: Competing with the colonial scalpel: ‘Peaceful atoms’ in Cold War Taiwan
candidates.abstract: This paper examines competing treatments-surgery and radioactive iodine (RAI, I131)-for hyperthyroidism in the context of post-colonial Cold War nuclear science in Taiwan. Although the U.S.-led Cold War Atoms for Peace project pushed for the globalization of nuclear medicine, it had to compete with the Japanese colonial legacy in Taiwan (Republic of China). This government-in-exile embraced nuclear science and ushered in RAI with staged rituals. However, this modern procedure failed to overtake the surgical approach (thyroidectomy); in fact, as late as the 1990s, well after RAI had become a standard procedure throughout the world, surgery was still the major treatment option for this common disease in Taiwan. The tension between the global and the local is rooted in infrastructure as well as the materiality, regulation and availability of the Iodine 131 isotope, and, finally, the customary practice of the surgical tradition, established since the colonial period. Thyroid diseases, especially endemic goiter, were an important issue in colonial medicine, and the study, diagnosis, and treatments of thyroid diseases were an integral part of colonial surgeons' identity. Surgical clinics had been a fixture of institutional medicine throughout Taiwan by the mid-twentieth century. In contrast, with the exception of a few prestigious hospitals in Taipei such as the National Taiwan University Hospital, most medical institutions and clinicians were not equipped to use isotopes. The availability of I131 was also limited, as the nuclear reactor did not become active until the 1960s. The preference for surgery thus points to the significance of material and social conditions of medical practice in Taiwan, amid the backdrop of the haunting images of the atomic bombs dropped by the U.S. on nearby Japan which the Atoms for Peace Project had aimed to overcome.

candidates.title: Morphometric mapping and social-factor weighting analysis of Ming export bowls
candidates.abstract: During China’s Ming dynasty, export porcelain played a central material role, yet how export-ware forms evolved in response to market demand, esthetic preference remains insufficiently understood. Focusing on porcelain bowls exported via the Lingnan region, this study combines morphometric mapping with a weighted analysis of socio-historical factors. The results are as follows. 1) Vessel height and rim diameter exhibit convergence, reflecting standardization driven by maritime transport and large-scale production, with foot rings present on 97% of samples. 2) Variation concentrates at the foot–wall junction, where angular adjustments correspond to different ergonomic and cultural preferences. 3) Economic forces (weighting 33%) dominate production scale, cultural preferences (23.7%) shape localized formal adaptation, political regulation 17.5% constrain decorative choices, and technical innovation 25.9% enable refinement. This study offer a replicable quantitative pathway for linking ceramic form to socio-economic drivers, contributing to a more integrated understanding of export porcelain within early global trade systems.

candidates.title: Remote work comes with a cost: An experimental videoconferencing study with motor-coordination, creative, and problem-solving tasks
candidates.abstract: Videoconferencing is used by millions to work and collaborate remotely, yet most theoretical research is decades old, and empirical studies on contemporary technology are scarce. In a comparative experimental study, we tested 40 dyads of Psychology students in four tasks (Alternate Uses Test, Desert Survival Situation, Tower of London, Key-Pressing), to find out how videoconferencing-mediated collaboration affects task performance (RQ1) and human subjective experience of the collaboration (RQ2), compared to face-to-face collaboration. We compared task scores by statistical between-group testing and found significant differences in the Tower of London (TOL) and Key-Pressing (Tapping) task. In the TOL, the videoconferencing dyads solved the tasks in significantly fewer moves than the face-to-face group, but needed significantly more time. In the Tapping, the face-to-face group achieved significantly more synchronous key-presses. Regarding their subjective collaboration experience, participants in the face-to-face condition felt significantly more co-present with their dyad partner, yet videoconferencing reported significantly stronger feelings of Perceived Attentional Engagement and Behavioral Interdependence. By interpreting the differences identified in our results, we have formulated four central insights: (1) Comparable performance can be achieved in videoconferencing-mediated collaboration. (2) Videoconferencing-mediated collaboration costs more time and mutual focus than face-to-face collaboration. (3) Tasks that require exact coordination and rely strongly on non-verbal communication can be impacted negatively by videoconferencing-mediated collaboration. (4) By demanding more explicit communication, videoconferencing-mediated collaboration may improve performance in some tasks. Our results may inform technology design and inspire the development of effective ways of using videoconferencing in collaborative activities.

candidates.title: From detection to action: artificial intelligence in integrated pest and invasive plant management
candidates.abstract: Global agriculture faces growing threats from pests, pathogens, and invasive species, intensified by climate change and biodiversity losses. Conventional approaches are limited in both precision and scale, and artificial intelligence (AI) is now reshaping integrated pest management (IPM). Modern agricultural monitoring leverages high-resolution observations, hyperspectral sensors, and the Internet of Things (IoT) to facilitate early detection for diseases. Hybrid AI systems can integrate multi-source data to enhance the accuracy of real-time monitoring of pest and disease dynamics, including the detection and tracking of sparse invasive populations and their biomass even under shifting climate scenarios. They further enable predictive forecasting and the optimization of management strategies. When AI-driven diagnostics are integrated with autonomous robotics, they form a robust framework for epidemic mitigation. Here, we provide a systematic macro-perspective review, bridging foundational AI mechanisms with actionable IPM intelligence. We analyze the evolution of agricultural AI from cross-modal architectures to multi-scale diagnostics and full-lifecycle interventions. Finally, we propose a framework for the global agroecological network, offering a sustainable path toward maximizing productivity while ensuring ecological resilience.

candidates.title: “Doing Right by Rory”: Affective, Ritualized, and Ethical Practices at the 2024 Rory Gallagher Collection Auction
candidates.abstract: In 2024, the estate of the late Irish blues-rock musician Rory Gallagher announced that his personal instrument collection would be offered for sale at the London auction house Bonhams. As a site of highly charged fan engagement, auctions provide a unique lens through which to examine the intersection of music material objects with affective, ritualized, and ethical practices. Drawing on object-oriented interviews with auction participants and informed by frameworks from affect theory and material culture studies, this paper conceptualizes the auction as a collective rite of passage rather than a purely economic transaction. In doing so, it highlights how material artifacts function as morally weighted technologies of presence, sustaining Gallagher’s posthumous legacy, and how fans approach the instruments as stewards rather than collectors, participating in a fan-led moral economy of acquisition and preservation. The auction, thus, can be seen as a form of “heritage-as-praxis” in which the movement of objects generates new performances of community, ethical regimes of value, and collective responsibility.
